title: Your landlord's management company offers a C$100 rent credit for a 'Love my building!' review.

outcomes.text: 'Teddy is a hero. The radiator plays trombone at 3 AM.' Three stars. The credit evaporates like the hot water.

later.text: Remember your honest review of the building? Teddy showed it to the owners and finally got the radiator part approved. Silence. Glorious silence.

options.label: Five stars for C$100
options.cost: A lie on your building's listing

outcomes.text: 'A peaceful home!' you type, as the radiator honks. C$100 credit. The radiator honks again, louder.

later.text: Remember your 'Love my building!' review? It's on the listing now, with your first name. Your new neighbor in 2B wants to talk about the radiator.

options.label: Five stars for Teddy only
options.riskWhy: They might not get the joke

outcomes.text: 'Teddy: five stars. Radiator: one. Average: Teddy.' No credit. Teddy prints it and tapes it to his folding chair.

title: Teddy asks you to tell the owners the leak in your ceiling is 'handled.' It's a bucket.

outcomes.text: 'It's a bucket.' The owners promise a roofer. Teddy says 'okay' in a tone that will haunt the hallway for days.

later.text: Remember telling the owners the leak was a bucket? The roofer came. Teddy admitted, at his folding chair, that you were right. Then he fixed your drawer.

options.label: Cover for Teddy
options.cost: A bucket in your ceiling, longer

outcomes.text: 'Handled!' you tell the owners. Teddy winks. The bucket goes 'plink.'

later.text: Remember telling the owners the leak was 'handled'? The bucket overflowed onto your C$70 sneakers. Teddy brought you a towel and a guilty look.

options.label: Truth, and stick up for Teddy
options.get: A fix, and Teddy off the hook

outcomes.text: 'It's a bucket, and Teddy's asked for a roofer six times.' Silence on the line. Then: 'We'll send someone.' Teddy hears and nods.

title: You borrowed Priya's good umbrella and the wind on 31st Street ate it. Priya texts: 'Seen my umbrella?'

outcomes.text: 'I killed it. I'm sorry. New one on the fridge.' Priya: 'You owe me a story about the wind.' Fair.

options.label: 'Haven't seen it'
options.cost: A small lie to your roommate
options.riskWhy: The pieces are in your trash

outcomes.text: 'Nope, haven't seen it.' Priya sends a sad emoji and blames Jersey. Your trash can is very quiet.

later.text: Remember 'haven't seen it'? Priya found her umbrella's skeleton in your trash. She's taped a sign to the fridge: 'Honesty is free.'

outcomes.text: You buy the same umbrella and hang it on the hook. Priya: 'Huh, it looks new.' You: 'Wild.'

title: You borrowed Mr. Florakis's step stool from 3A and snapped a leg. He's in the hallway, asking around.

options.label: Own up and offer to pay
options.riskWhy: He may tell a long story

outcomes.text: 'That was me.' Mr. Florakis waves off your money, then accepts it, then tells you about the stool's history since 1974.

later.text: Remember owning up about Mr. Florakis's step stool? He left a spanakopita at your door, with a note: 'For the honest one, from 3A.'

options.label: Get Teddy to fix it first
options.get: A fixed stool, maybe no questions

outcomes.text: Teddy glues it in ten minutes and charges you C$20 and a raised eyebrow. The stool goes back, stronger than before.

options.label: Lean it back by his door
options.cost: A neighbor's stool, and his knees

outcomes.text: You lean the stool by 3A's door and tiptoe away. The broken leg is facing the wall. That's a choice.

later.text: Remember leaning the broken stool by 3A's door? Mr. Florakis wobbled, caught himself, and told the whole building. Everyone looks at you on the stairs.

title: The building group chat: 'Who was blasting music at 2 AM?' It was you. 4B is getting blamed.

options.label: 'That was me, sorry'
options.riskWhy: The chat roasts you for a day

outcomes.text: 'That was me, sorry all.' Thirty thumbs-down, one heart from 4B. Teddy replies 'thank you' with no punctuation.

later.text: Remember owning up to the 2 AM music? 4B invited you to their name-day party. Andreas catered. You danced, at a reasonable volume.

options.label: Say nothing
options.riskWhy: Walls are thin, so are alibis

outcomes.text: You watch the chat pile on 4B. You put on a podcast about ethics, then turn it off.

later.text: Remember staying quiet while 4B got blamed for the 2 AM music? Teddy heard it from the hallway. He posted: 'It was not 4B.'

options.label: Pile on 4B too
options.riskWhy: Teddy knows whose music it was

outcomes.text: 'Honestly, 4B, some of us work.' Fifteen likes. 4B leaves the chat.

later.text: Remember piling on 4B for your own 2 AM music? Teddy posted a voice memo from the hallway. It's your playlist. 4B rejoined the chat just to react.

title: Teddy holds up a pizza box in the recycling, still full of crusts: 'Whose is this?' It's yours.

options.label: 'Mine, I'll fix it'
options.riskWhy: The bin is gross, that's all

outcomes.text: You sort the bin while Teddy supervises from his folding chair and explains which plastic is which. All of them, apparently.
'Not sure, Teddy.' He looks at the box. The box says 'Still-a-Dollar Slice.' You get Still-a-Dollar Slice every day.

later.text: Remember shrugging at Teddy about the pizza box? He taped it to your door with a note: 'Not sure either.' The whole floor walked past it.

options.label: 'Probably 4B'
options.riskWhy: There's a receipt on the box

outcomes.text: 'Probably 4B.' Teddy heads for the stairs with the box. You feel the receipt taped to its lid in your bones.

later.text: Remember blaming 4B for the pizza box? The receipt on the lid had your name and order. Teddy gave it to 4B, who gave it to the group chat.
